response.title: which solar inverter can start the biggest motor
response.answer:
The best solar inverter for starting a large motor is not necessarily the inverter with the highest continuous wattage. The most important specification is its surge capacity and ability to handle motor inrush current.

For example, a 10 HP motor might require only 8–10 kW while running, but could briefly demand 40–70 kVA or more when starting directly across the line.

For large motors, I would compare three things:

Surge power: How much power the inverter can deliver for a few seconds.

Surge duration: Whether it can sustain the motor's starting current long enough to accelerate.

Motor-starting method: Direct-on-line (DOL), soft starter, or variable-frequency drive (VFD).

A VFD can dramatically reduce the inverter capacity needed to start a large motor.

Strong residential candidates
Shop

SOL-ARK 15K-2P 15kW 120/240/208 48V All-In-One Pre-Wired Hyb…

12 kW battery-only continuous · 24 kVA for 10 seconds · 30 kVA for 100 ms (earlier datasheet)

A strong choice for large residential motors and pumps. Multiple units can be paralleled. 
Sol-Ark
+1

$5,299.00

Shop

EG4 18kPV Hybrid Inverter | EG4-18kPV-12LV | 48V Split Phase…

12 kW continuous · 13.5 kW for 10 minutes (reported overload rating)

A lower-cost alternative, but its published overload figure alone does not establish that it can start a larger motor than the Sol-Ark. 
Paravolta

$3,999.99

For a much larger motor, a parallel inverter system or commercial three-phase inverter system may be necessary. Sol-Ark documents up to 12 parallel 15K units, with a combined nominal 10-second surge rating of 288 kVA, although that does not guarantee starting a motor requiring that much inrush current. 
Amazon Web Services, Inc.

My preliminary pick for a single residential inverter is the Sol-Ark 15K, but I cannot establish it as the worldwide leader for motor starting.
